messages.subject: Questions about Matrix C
messages.body_plain:
Hi, Dr. Jiang,

Thanks for your contribution with such a great software tool Canopy.

After reading all illustrations about matrix C, I still can't understand it.

For example, in MDA231 sample data, I guess chr7_1 and chr7_2 overlapped with each other. however, there are no more information about chr7_1 and chr7_2.
I can't find any numbers related to these two symbols from matrix X, Y, WM, Wm,R.

Could you kindly explain it more detailedly?

Thanks

Chuan Jiang

messages.subject: Re: [canopy_phylogeny] Questions about Matrix C
messages.body_plain:
Hi Chuan,

Thanks for your interest in Canopy and sorry for my late reply — I just got back from travel. Here is a more detailed explanation on how to generate the C matrix: https://github.com/yuchaojiang/Canopy/blob/master/instruction/overlapping_CNA.md .

Specifically, for this dataset, we know chr7 has two CNA events (supplementary Figure S13) with different breakpoints. However for this CNA region in Figure S13, we only have one CNA input for a specific sample, i.e., we won’t know the chr7_1 and chr7_2 input for each sample until we perform the deconvolution.

I am working on more detailed illustration on overlapping CNAs and I hope to push the update onto GitHub soon. Also please update your package via GitHub — I made significant changes last week.

Feel free to let me know if you have further questions.

Best,
Yuchao

messages.subject: Re: [canopy_phylogeny] Questions about Matrix C
messages.body_plain:
Yes that is theoratically correct. Although whole genome doubling event can be hard to detect and in this case it can be even harder to let the algorithm deconvolute itself. You can definitely try this though and see if the results make sense.

One way to make this easier if you are sure that the doubling event is true is to fix a genome-wide doubling event at the first split of the tree so that all subsequent events happen after this. This is not enabled by Canopy though you might have to zoom into the source code and modify a bit.

Yuchao

messages.subject: Re: [canopy_phylogeny] Tumor evolution using SNAs
messages.body_plain:
Thanks for your interest in Canopy! Yes you only need R and X (R/X is your observed VAF, i.e., what you also have) to infer phylogeny using SNAs only.

realZ, realP, realVAF are the real quantities that we simulate R and X from, which is used as a gold standard.

Mu, Tau, sna_cluster is from pre-clustering step, which is optional but is recommended if you have many SNAs and they form clusters by visual check. See here https://github.com/yuchaojiang/Canopy/tree/master/clustering for more details.

If you have Mu, Tau, sna_cluster, use canopy.sample.cluster.nocna; if you don’t perform pre-clustering, use canopy.sample.nocna. More details can be found here https://github.com/yuchaojiang/Canopy/blob/master/instruction/sampling_mode.md.

Hope that this clarifies. A side note is that if you are using only SNAs as input, you should exclude all SNAs with VAF > 50% since they have to be within CNA regions, which you don’t have input of. Also from our experience multiple tree configurations can be possible especially if only SNAs are used as input, thus you should definitely increase the number of chains in the sampling steps so that as much tree space as possible is sampled.

Hope that this clarifies and let me know if you have further questions.

Yuchao

messages.subject: Re: [canopy_phylogeny] Pre-clustering step in Canopy
messages.body_plain:
Hi Victor,

When you get the column from R and X, it changes it to a vector instead of a matrix. This leads to the error that you saw. Canopy is primary for >=2 samples and for the clustering code I had we initialize the EM with k-means based on euclidean and correlation distance. Correlation won’t work for your case since it is only 1d. I modified the code though so you can run it through. Please update / reinstall Canopy from our GitHub page. The code I used is attached.

Also, I want to mention again that clustering is not the major contribution of Canopy but only a by-product. We don’t devote much time developing or maintaining it. Therefore, if you are working on benchmarking clustering algorithms, I think think it is fair to include Canopy. You can refer to Pyclone and SciClone which specifically tackle this issue.

All the best,
Yuchao

messages.body_plain:
Hi Jesse,

I just replied to another user with the same question yesterday. Please see below. Note that you need to update the package from GitHub. Canopy is not primarily designed for one sample  -- I’m not sure how much information about phylogeny you can get from one heterogeneous sample. Also Canopy is not focused on clustering, which is only a by-product of the program.

Thanks,

Yuchao
